speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: In New Mexico,

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: if you're walking home alone after midnight,

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: and a woman in black is standing at the crossroads...

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: keep walking.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Because she isn't waiting for a ride.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: She's waiting to tell you who's next.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: They call her La Mala Hora.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: The evil hour.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Her story is told in Hispanic communities across New Mexico,

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: where white crosses called descansos line the back roads.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Each one marks a place where someone died.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: According to the legend, she appears to people traveling alone at night,

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: right where two roads meet.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: She never touches you.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: She doesn't have to.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: But here's the terrifying part.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Seeing her doesn't mean you'll die.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: It means someone you love will.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: One woman saw her at a crossroads.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: By morning, she learned her husband had died...

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: at that exact hour.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: They say she doesn't always look human.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Sometimes she's just a dark shape rolling across the road.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: So if you're walking home alone tonight,

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: don't stop, and don't look back.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Because she isn't there for you.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: She's there to tell you who's not coming home.
